rows.label: 能愿动词 (敢)

lesson.title: 敢: to dare to do something
lesson.summary: 敢 is a modal verb meaning "dare to"; it goes before the verb and is negated with 不敢 (or 没敢 for a past moment).
pattern: A + 不敢 / 没敢 + V
A + 敢 + V + 吗？ / A + 敢不敢 + V？
body: 敢 (gǎn) is a modal verb: it stands before another verb and says that someone has the courage to do it. 他什么都敢试 means he dares to try anything. The usual negative is 不敢 (does not dare); for one moment in the past, 没敢 is also common: 我没敢问他. Questions are 你敢跳吗？ or 你敢不敢跳？. A sentence with nobody as the subject, 没人敢……, means nobody dares.
The contrast example uses 勇敢 (brave), an adjective. 勇敢 describes a person (一个很勇敢的孩子) and cannot take a verb after it; 敢 is the modal verb that takes the verb.
Common mistake: 我不勇敢一个人睡. Use the modal verb: 我不敢一个人睡.

rows.label: 指示代词 (各, 各位, 各种, 任何, 此)

lesson.title: 各 各位 各种 任何 此: each, all kinds, any, this
lesson.summary: 各 means each of a group, 各位 addresses a group politely, 各种 means all kinds of, 任何 means any at all, and 此 is a formal word for this.
pattern: 任何 + N + 都 / 也 …
body: 各 (gè) before a noun or measure word means each member of a group: 各国 (every country), 各个班. 各位 (gèwèi) is a polite way to address a group: 各位同学, 各位老师. 各种 (gè zhǒng) means all kinds of: 各种水果. 任何 (rènhé) means any at all; it usually comes with 都 or 也, or after a negative: 任何人都不能进去, 没有任何问题.
此 (cǐ) is the formal, written word for this. It is used mostly in set words: 从此 (from then on), 此时 (at this moment), 因此 (therefore).

The contrast example uses 每 (each, every), from HSK 2. 每 goes with a measure word and usually 都: 每个人都有一张票. 各 is more formal and often goes straight before the noun (各国); 任何 stresses that there is no exception.
Common mistake: 这家店卖任何水果. 任何 does not go in a plain affirmative object; say 这家店卖各种水果, or 任何水果都有.

rows.label: 专用名量词 (打, 袋, 棵, 台, 幅)

lesson.title: Special measure words: 打 袋 棵 台 幅
lesson.summary: Some nouns take their own measure word: 打 for a dozen, 袋 for a bag of, 棵 for trees and plants, 台 for machines, 幅 for pictures.
pattern: number + 打 / 袋 / 棵 / 台 / 幅 + N
body: These measure words belong to particular nouns. 打 (dá) is a dozen: 一打鸡蛋. 袋 (dài) is a bag of something: 两袋面包, 一袋米. 棵 (kē) counts trees and plants: 三棵树, 一棵草. 台 (tái) counts machines: 一台电脑, 两台空调. 幅 (fú) counts pictures, paintings and maps: 一幅画.
The contrast example uses 个, the general measure word from HSK 1. 个 goes with many nouns (一个主意, 一个人), but with a tree, a computer or a painting a speaker expects 棵, 台 or 幅.
Common mistake: 一个树 or 一个电脑. Say 一棵树, 一台电脑.

rows.label: 借用名量词 (脸, 手, 盒, 屋子, 桌子)

lesson.title: Borrowed measure words: 一脸 一手 一盒 一屋子 一桌子
lesson.summary: A noun such as 脸, 手, 盒, 屋子 or 桌子 can work as a measure word: 一盒 is a box of, and 一脸, 一手, 一屋子, 一桌子 mean a face, a hand, a room or a table full of.
pattern: 一 + 脸 / 手 / 屋子 / 桌子 + N (full of, all over)
body: A container or a body part can be borrowed as a measure word. 盒 (hé) is a box of: 一盒巧克力, 两盒牛奶. With 一, the words 脸 (liǎn), 手 (shǒu), 屋子 (wūzi) and 桌子 (zhuōzi) mean the whole face, hand, room or table is covered or filled: 一脸不高兴 (a face full of displeasure), 一手油 (oily hands), 一屋子客人 (a roomful of guests), 一桌子菜 (a table covered with dishes).
The contrast example uses 张, the measure word for the noun 桌子: 二十张桌子. There 桌子 is the thing being counted; in 一桌子菜 it is the measure word, and the thing is 菜.
Common mistake: 两桌子菜 to mean a table full of dishes. The full-of reading needs 一; with other numbers 桌 counts tables at a banquet (两桌菜).

rows.label: 动量词 (场, 顿, 趟)

lesson.title: Verbal measure words 场 顿 趟: a spell of, a meal or scolding, a trip
lesson.summary: 场 counts a spell of rain or illness and whole events, 顿 counts meals and scoldings, and 趟 counts trips there and back.
pattern: V + (了) + number + 场 / 顿 / 趟 (+ N)
body: These measure words count how many times an action happens, and each suits certain verbs. 场 (cháng) counts a spell of weather or illness: 下了一场大雨, 生了一场病. Read 场 as chǎng when it counts a whole show or match: 一场电影, 一场比赛. 顿 (dùn) counts meals and also beatings or scoldings: 吃一顿饭, 骂了他一顿. 趟 (tàng) counts trips to a place and back: 去一趟银行, 跑一趟.
The contrast example uses 次, the general verbal measure word from HSK 2: 再说一次. 次 just counts times; 场, 顿 and 趟 add what kind of event it was.
Common mistake: 我去了一次趟北京. Use one measure word: 我去了一趟北京.

rows.label: 程度副词 (十分, 更加, 稍, 稍微, 尤其, 多么)

lesson.title: Degree adverbs 十分 更加 稍微 尤其 多么
lesson.summary: 十分 means very, 更加 means even more, 稍 and 稍微 mean a little, 尤其 means especially, and 多么 makes an exclamation.
pattern: 稍 / 稍微 + V / Adj + 一点儿 / 一下 / 有点儿
body: 十分 (shífēn) is a written-style very: 十分高兴. 更加 (gèngjiā) is a fuller form of 更, even more, often in comparisons over time: 空气更加新鲜了. 稍 (shāo) and 稍微 (shāowēi) mean slightly; they rarely stand alone and usually take 一点儿, 一下 or 有点儿: 稍等一下, 稍微有点儿大.
尤其 (yóuqí) picks out one item from a group: 我喜欢运动，尤其是游泳. 多么 (duōme) makes an exclamation and normally ends with 啊: 多么美啊！. It does not go in a plain statement.
The contrast example uses 有点儿 (a bit, usually for something unwelcome), from HSK 2: 今天有点儿冷. It goes before the adjective; 一点儿 goes after it (冷一点儿), so 今天一点儿冷 is wrong.
Common mistake: 多么 in a plain statement, as in 这里多么美. Make it an exclamation with 啊 (这里多么美啊！), or use 十分 for a statement.

rows.label: 范围副词 (共, 全, 光, 仅, 仅仅, 至少)

lesson.title: Scope adverbs 共 全 光 仅 仅仅 至少: in all, entirely, only, at least
lesson.summary: 共 means in all, 全 means entirely or all, 光 and 仅 / 仅仅 mean only, and 至少 means at least.
pattern: 光 / 仅 / 仅仅 / 至少 + V / number
body: 共 (gòng) is the short written form of 一共, in all: 这本书共有十二课. 全 (quán) says all of the group or the whole thing: 他们全都来了. 光 (guāng) is a spoken only, often in advice: 不能光吃肉. 仅 (jǐn) and 仅仅 (jǐnjǐn) are formal only and stress how little: 仅用了三天, 他仅仅是个孩子. 至少 (zhìshǎo) means at least: 至少要喝八杯水.
The contrast example uses 只 (only), the everyday word from HSK 2: 我只带了十块钱. 光, 仅 and 仅仅 are its spoken and formal relatives; 至少 is the opposite direction, a lower limit.
Common mistake: 全 for in total. 全班 means the whole class; for a sum, use 共 or 一共: 一共三十人.

rows.label: 时间副词 (按时, 从来, 从, 本来, 已)

lesson.title: Time adverbs 按时 从来 从 本来 已: on time, ever, originally, already
lesson.summary: 按时 means on time, 从来 and 从 with a negative mean never, 本来 means originally, and 已 is the written form of 已经.
pattern: 从来 / 从 + 不 / 没 + V
本来 + V …, (后来 / 可是 …)
body: 按时 (ànshí) means at the set time: 按时吃药, 按时交作业. 从来 (cónglái) means ever, and nearly always comes with a negative: 从来不 for a habit, 从来没 (……过) for experience: 我从来没去过国外. The single word 从 does the same in writing: 他从不喝酒.
本来 (běnlái) means originally, at first, and the next clause usually says what changed: 我本来想去，后来有事没去成. 已 (yǐ) is the short, formal form of 已经: 飞机已到达北京.
The contrast example uses 一直 (all along, continuously), from HSK 2: 他一直住在北京. 一直 works in an affirmative sentence; 从来 usually needs a negative, so 他从来住在北京 is wrong.
Common mistake: 我从来去过上海. Add the negative, 我从来没去过上海, or use 一直 or 常常 for a positive habit.

rows.label: 时间副词 (赶紧, 赶快, 忽然, 将, 将要)

lesson.title: Time adverbs 赶紧 赶快 忽然 将 将要: hurry, suddenly, will
lesson.summary: 赶紧 and 赶快 urge someone to hurry, 忽然 says something happened suddenly, and 将 / 将要 mark the future in a formal way.
pattern: 将 / 将要 + V (+ 了)
body: 赶紧 (gǎnjǐn) and 赶快 (gǎnkuài) mean hurry up and do it, often in suggestions or commands: 我们赶紧回家吧, 你赶快去医院看看. 忽然 (hūrán) says an event happened without warning: 忽然停电了, 他忽然想起一件事. 将 (jiāng) and 将要 (jiāngyào) are formal markers of the future: 新学期将在九月开始, 火车将要进站了.

There are two contrast examples. 突然 (sudden) can be an adjective as well as an adverb: 这个消息太突然了. 忽然 is only an adverb, so 太忽然了 is wrong. 马上 (right away), from HSK 2, is the everyday word for an action about to happen: 我马上就来; 将要 belongs to announcements and writing.
Common mistake: 赶快 for something that happens by itself, as in 赶快下雨了. 赶快 needs a person who hurries; for weather use 快要下雨了.

rows.label: 频率副词 (重新, 往往, 偶尔, 再次, 老)

lesson.title: Frequency adverbs 重新 往往 偶尔 再次 老: again, usually, occasionally, always
lesson.summary: 重新 means do over again, 往往 says what usually happens in a situation, 偶尔 means occasionally, 再次 means once more, and 老 complains that something keeps happening.
pattern: A + 往往 / 偶尔 / 老 + V
body: 重新 (chóngxīn) means start again and do it differently or from the beginning: 请重新写一遍. 往往 (wǎngwǎng) states what tends to happen under certain conditions, from experience: 年轻人往往睡得很晚; it is not used for a single future plan. 偶尔 (ǒu'ěr) means now and then: 我偶尔也会喝一点儿咖啡. 再次 (zàicì) is a formal once again: 他再次获得了第一名.
老 (lǎo) before a verb means always, in a complaining tone: 你怎么老忘关灯？, 这几天老是下雨. This 老 is an adverb, not the prefix in 老王.
The contrast example uses 又 (again), from HSK 2: 他昨天来了，今天又来了. 又 is for a repeat that has already happened; 再 is for one that has not, so 今天再来了 is wrong. 再次 is the formal word and works for both.
Common mistake: 我往往明天去 for a plan. 往往 is for a pattern you have seen; for a plan use 常常 or a time word.

rows.label: 方式副词 (故意, 互相, 相互)

lesson.title: 故意 互相 相互: on purpose, each other
lesson.summary: 故意 means on purpose; 互相 and 相互 mean each other, with 相互 the more formal one.
pattern: A 和 B / plural subject + 互相 / 相互 + V
body: 故意 (gùyì) says someone did something on purpose, often something unkind: 他故意不接我的电话. 我不是故意的 is the usual way to say it was an accident.

互相 (hùxiāng) and 相互 (xiānghù) say that each person does the action to the other, so the subject is plural: 兄弟俩从小就互相照顾. 相互 is more formal and can also stand before 的 and a noun: 相互的理解. In everyday speech 互相 is far more common.
The contrast example uses 一起 (together), from HSK 1: 我们一起去打篮球吧. 一起 says people do the same thing side by side; 互相 says they do it to one another, so 我们互相去打篮球 is wrong.
Common mistake: 他互相帮助我. 互相 needs a plural subject and no object for the other person: 我们互相帮助.

examples.translation: The two brothers have looked after each other since they were small.

examples.text: 我们要相互学习，共同进步。
examples.reading: wǒmen yào xiānghù xuéxí, gòngtóng jìnbù.
examples.translation: We should learn from each other and make progress together.

examples.text: 这两个问题是相互影响的。
examples.reading: zhè liǎng ge wèntí shì xiānghù yǐngxiǎng de.
examples.translation: These two problems affect each other.

examples.reading: tāmen liǎ hùxiāng kàn le yì yǎn.
examples.translation: The two of them glanced at each other.

examples.reading: wǒmen yìqǐ qù dǎ lánqiú ba.
examples.translation: Let us go and play basketball together.

rows.label: 关联副词 (却)

lesson.title: 却: but, yet (after the subject)
lesson.summary: 却 is an adverb meaning but or yet; it goes after the subject of the second clause, where 但是 goes before it.
body: 却 (què) marks a result that goes against what the first clause leads you to expect: 天气很冷，他却只穿了一件衬衫. Because it is an adverb, it stands after the subject and before the verb or adjective, never at the very front of the clause.
The contrast example uses the conjunction 但是 (but), from HSK 2: 他很聪明，但是他不努力. 但是 comes before the subject; 却 comes after it. The two can even appear together: 但是他却不努力.
Common mistake: 却他不愿意. Move 却 after the subject: 他却不愿意.

examples.text: 他学了三年汉语，水平却不太高。
examples.reading: tā xué le sān nián Hànyǔ, shuǐpíng què bú tài gāo.
examples.translation: He has studied Chinese for three years, yet his level is still not very high.

examples.text: 天气很冷，他却只穿了一件衬衫。
examples.reading: tiānqì hěn lěng, tā què zhǐ chuān le yí jiàn chènshān.
examples.translation: It is cold, yet he is wearing only a shirt.

examples.reading: wǒ xiǎng bāng tā, tā què bú yuànyì.
examples.translation: I wanted to help him, but he was not willing.

examples.reading: dōngxi bú guì, zhìliàng què hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: The goods are cheap, yet the quality is good.

examples.text: 大家都到了，他却还没来。
examples.reading: dàjiā dōu dào le, tā què hái méi lái.
examples.translation: Everyone has arrived, but he still has not come.

examples.text: 他很聪明，但是他不努力。
examples.reading: tā hěn cōngming, dànshì tā bù nǔlì.
examples.translation: He is clever, but he does not work hard.

rows.label: 情态副词 (也许, 恐怕)

lesson.title: 也许 and 恐怕: perhaps, I am afraid that
lesson.summary: 也许 means perhaps; 恐怕 also means probably but adds worry that the outcome is unwelcome.
pattern: A + 也许 / 恐怕 + V
body: 也许 (yěxǔ) makes a guess: 也许是我记错了. 恐怕 (kǒngpà) makes a guess about something you do not want: 恐怕要下雨了, 这件事恐怕不太好办. Both are adverbs that can stand at the front of the sentence or right after the subject, so 老师也许还在办公室 and 也许老师还在办公室 are both correct.
The contrast example uses the verb 害怕 (to be afraid of): 妹妹很害怕大狗. 害怕 takes an object and can follow 很; 恐怕 is only a guessing adverb, so 很恐怕大狗 is wrong.
Common mistake: 我恐怕狗. To fear something, use 怕 or 害怕: 我怕狗.

examples.text: 恐怕要下雨了，带上伞吧。
examples.reading: kǒngpà yào xià yǔ le, dài shang sǎn ba.
examples.translation: I am afraid it is going to rain; take an umbrella.

examples.reading: yěxǔ shì wǒ jì cuò le.
examples.translation: Perhaps I remembered it wrong.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì kǒngpà bú tài hǎo bàn.
examples.translation: I am afraid this will not be easy to sort out.

examples.reading: xiànzài qù kǒngpà yǐjīng wǎn le.
examples.translation: I am afraid it is already too late to go now.

examples.reading: lǎoshī yěxǔ hái zài bàngōngshì.
examples.translation: The teacher may still be in the office.

examples.reading: mèimei hěn hàipà dà gǒu.
examples.translation: My younger sister is very scared of big dogs.

rows.label: 语气副词 (才, 就, 并, 还)

lesson.title: Mood uses of 才 就 并 还: insisting, denying, reproaching
lesson.summary: Besides their time meanings, 才 and 就 add emphasis, 并 before a negative denies what someone assumed, and 还 in 还……呢 reproaches.
pattern: 并 + 不 / 没 + V; 还 + N / V + 呢
body: 才 (cái) can insist or contradict: 我才不跟他去呢！ (I certainly will not), 这才是我想要的生活 (this, and nothing less, is the life I want). 就 (jiù) can stress that it is exactly this and nothing else: 我就要这件, 银行就在超市对面.
并 (bìng) before 不 or 没 denies an assumption: 这道题并不难 (it is not hard at all, whatever you think). 还 (hái) in 还……呢 reproaches someone for falling short of what they should be: 你还是哥哥呢，怎么不帮帮妹妹？
The contrast example uses 才 in its time meaning, from HSK 3: 会议九点才开始 (not until nine). There 才 says later than expected; in 我才不去呢 it is pure emphasis.
Common mistake: 这道题并难. 并 in this sense needs a negative after it: 并不难, 并没有.

examples.reading: wǒ cái bù gēn tā qù ne!
examples.translation: I am certainly not going with him!

examples.reading: zhè cái shì wǒ xiǎng yào de shēnghuó.
examples.translation: This is the life I really want.

examples.text: 我就要这件，别的都不要。
examples.reading: wǒ jiù yào zhè jiàn, bié de dōu bú yào.
examples.translation: I want this one and no other.

examples.reading: yínháng jiù zài chāoshì duìmiàn.
examples.translation: The bank is right across from the supermarket.

examples.text: 这道题并不难，你再想想。
examples.reading: zhè dào tí bìng bù nán, nǐ zài xiǎngxiang.
examples.translation: This question is not hard at all; think again.

examples.text: 你还是哥哥呢，怎么不帮帮妹妹？
examples.reading: nǐ hái shì gēge ne, zěnme bù bāngbang mèimei?
examples.translation: And you call yourself her big brother? Why will you not help your little sister?

examples.reading: huìyì jiǔ diǎn cái kāishǐ.
examples.translation: The meeting does not start until nine.

rows.label: 语气副词 (竟然, 究竟, 到底, 难道)

lesson.title: 竟然 究竟 到底 难道: surprise, pressing questions, rhetorical questions
lesson.summary: 竟然 says something is surprising, 究竟 and 到底 press for the real answer in a question, and 难道 starts a rhetorical question ending in 吗.
pattern: 究竟 / 到底 + question word …？
body: 竟然 (jìngrán) says the fact goes beyond what you expected: 他竟然一个人做完了. 究竟 (jiūjìng) and 到底 (dàodǐ) go into a question with a question word or an A-not-A form and demand the real answer: 你究竟想去哪儿？, 这到底是怎么回事？. They are not used with 吗. 到底 can also mean in the end, after all: 他到底还是来了.
难道 (nándào) opens a rhetorical question and the sentence normally ends in 吗: 难道你忘了明天要考试吗？ means surely you have not forgotten. 难道 is not used with a question word such as 哪儿.
The contrast example uses 原来 (so that is how it is), from HSK 3: 原来他是你哥哥！. 原来 marks finding out the truth; 竟然 marks being surprised by it.
Common mistake: 你到底去不去吗？. 到底 already makes the question; drop 吗: 你到底去不去？

examples.reading: tā jìngrán yí ge rén zuò wán le.
examples.translation: He actually finished it all by himself.

examples.text: 他平时很少锻炼，竟然跑了第一名。
examples.reading: tā píngshí hěn shǎo duànliàn, jìngrán pǎo le dì-yī míng.
examples.translation: He hardly ever exercises, yet he actually came first in the race.

examples.reading: nǐ jiūjìng xiǎng qù nǎr?
examples.translation: Where exactly do you want to go?

examples.reading: zhè dàodǐ shì zěnme huí shì?
examples.translation: What on earth is going on?

examples.text: 难道你忘了明天要考试吗？
examples.reading: nándào nǐ wàng le míngtiān yào kǎoshì ma?
examples.translation: Surely you have not forgotten there is an exam tomorrow?

examples.reading: nándào bú shì ma?
examples.translation: Is it not so?

examples.reading: tā dàodǐ háishi lái le.
examples.translation: He came after all.

examples.reading: yuánlái tā shì nǐ gēge!
examples.translation: So he is your brother!

rows.label: 语气副词 (正好, 千万, 确实, 只好, 差点儿)

lesson.title: 正好 千万 确实 只好 差点儿: just right, be sure to, indeed, had to, almost
lesson.summary: 正好 means just right or by luck, 千万 urges or warns, 确实 confirms, 只好 means there was no choice, and 差点儿 means almost.
pattern: 正好 + V / clause; V + 得 + 正好
千万 + 要 / 别 + V
确实 / 只好 / 差（一）点儿 + V
body: 正好 (zhènghǎo) says the timing or amount is just right, often by luck: 你来得正好, 我正好有空. 千万 (qiānwàn) strongly urges or warns and comes before 要, 别 or 不要: 你千万别告诉他. 确实 (quèshí) confirms that something really is so: 他说的确实是真的.
只好 (zhǐhǎo) says there was no better choice: 没有车了，我们只好走回家. 差点儿 (chàdiǎnr), also 差一点儿, says something almost happened but did not: 我差点儿迟到了, 我差一点儿忘了你的生日.
The contrast example uses 一定 (surely, must), from HSK 2: 他一定是生病了. 一定 can make a confident guess in a statement; 千万 only urges or warns, so 他千万是生病了 is wrong.
Common mistake: 千万去 with nothing between. Keep 要 or 别: 你千万要去.

examples.text: 你来得正好，帮我搬一下桌子。
examples.reading: nǐ lái de zhènghǎo, bāng wǒ bān yíxià zhuōzi.
examples.translation: You have come at just the right moment; help me move this table.

examples.reading: wǒ zhènghǎo yǒu kòng, péi nǐ qù ba.
examples.translation: I happen to be free; I will go with you.

examples.reading: nǐ qiānwàn bié gàosu tā.
examples.translation: Whatever you do, do not tell him.

examples.reading: tā shuō de quèshí shì zhēn de.
examples.translation: What he said really is true.

examples.text: 没有车了，我们只好走回家。
examples.reading: méiyǒu chē le, wǒmen zhǐhǎo zǒu huí jiā.
examples.translation: There were no more buses, so we had to walk home.

examples.reading: wǒ chàdiǎnr chídào le.
examples.translation: I was almost late.

examples.text: 我差一点儿忘了你的生日。
examples.reading: wǒ chà yìdiǎnr wàng le nǐ de shēngrì.
examples.translation: I almost forgot your birthday.

examples.reading: tā yídìng shì shēngbìng le.
examples.translation: He must be ill.

rows.label: 介词: 引出时间、处所 (自, 当, 由, 随着, 等)

lesson.title: 自 当 由 随着 等: from, when, along with, until
lesson.summary: 自 and 由 mark a starting point, 当……的时候 marks the moment something happens, 随着 means as something changes, and 等 means once or by the time something happens.
pattern: V + 自 + place; 自 + time + 起
当 + clause + 的时候 / 时
由 + place + V; 随着 + change; 等 + clause, (再 …)
body: 自 (zì) is a formal from. It often follows a verb, as in 来自上海, or opens a time phrase with 起: 自今天起. 由 (yóu) also marks a starting place: 我们由这里出发. 当 (dāng) frames the moment of an event with 的时候 or 时: 当我到家的时候，雨已经停了.

随着 (suízhe) means along with or as: the second clause changes because the first does: 随着天气变冷，感冒的人多了起来. 等 (děng) here is a preposition meaning once or by the time; the next clause usually has 再 or 就: 等你回来，我们再吃饭.
The contrast example uses 从 (from), from HSK 2: 他从小就喜欢画画. 从 is the everyday word for from; 自 and 由 are formal.
Common mistake: 当我到家，雨停了. 当 needs 的时候 or 时 to close the clause: 当我到家的时候.

examples.reading: tā láizì Shànghǎi.
examples.translation: He comes from Shanghai.

examples.text: 图书馆自今天起免费开放。
examples.reading: túshūguǎn zì jīntiān qǐ miǎnfèi kāifàng.
examples.translation: From today the library is open free of charge.

examples.text: 当我到家的时候，雨已经停了。
examples.reading: dāng wǒ dào jiā de shíhou, yǔ yǐjīng tíng le.
examples.translation: By the time I got home, the rain had stopped.

examples.reading: wǒmen yóu zhèlǐ chūfā.
examples.translation: We set off from here.

examples.text: 随着天气变冷，感冒的人多了起来。
examples.reading: suízhe tiānqì biàn lěng, gǎnmào de rén duō le qǐlai.
examples.translation: As the weather gets colder, more people are catching colds.

examples.reading: děng nǐ huílai, wǒmen zài chīfàn.
examples.translation: We will eat once you are back.

examples.reading: tā cóng xiǎo jiù xǐhuan huà huà.
examples.translation: He has loved drawing since he was little.

rows.label: 介词: 引出施事、受事 (将, 由, 叫, 让)

lesson.title: 将 由 叫 让: the formal 把, the person in charge, the passive doer
lesson.summary: 将 is a formal 把 that brings the object forward, 由 names the person responsible for an action, and 叫 and 让 introduce the doer in a spoken passive.
pattern: thing + 叫 / 让 + doer + V + other
body: 将 (jiāng) works like 把 in written or formal Chinese: 请将手机关掉, 他将这件事告诉了大家. As with 把, the verb needs something after it (掉, 了大家). 由 (yóu) names who is in charge of doing something: 这件事由我负责, 晚会由小李主持.
叫 (jiào) and 让 (ràng) make a spoken passive: the thing that is affected comes first and the doer follows 叫 or 让: 我的雨伞叫谁拿走了, 牛奶让猫喝光了. The doer must be named; use 人 when it is unknown.
The contrast example uses 被, the main passive marker from HSK 3: 他的钱包被偷了. 被 can drop the doer, as here; 叫 and 让 cannot.
Common mistake: 我的钱包让偷了. With 让 or 叫, name a doer: 我的钱包让人偷了.

examples.reading: qǐng jiāng shǒujī guān diào.
examples.translation: Please switch off your phones.

examples.text: 他将这件事告诉了大家。
examples.reading: tā jiāng zhè jiàn shì gàosu le dàjiā.
examples.translation: He told everyone about this.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì yóu wǒ fùzé.
examples.translation: I am in charge of this matter.

examples.reading: wǎnhuì yóu Xiǎo Lǐ zhǔchí.
examples.translation: The evening party is hosted by Xiao Li.

examples.reading: wǒ de yǔsǎn jiào shéi ná zǒu le?
examples.translation: Who has taken my umbrella?

examples.reading: niúnǎi ràng māo hē guāng le.
examples.translation: The milk was all drunk up by the cat.

examples.reading: tā de qiánbāo bèi tōu le.
examples.translation: His wallet was stolen.

rows.label: 介词: 引出原因 (由于)

lesson.title: 由于 + noun phrase: because of, owing to
lesson.summary: 由于 as a preposition puts a noun phrase in front of the sentence to give the cause: 由于大雾 (because of the fog).
body: 由于 (yóuyú) means because of. Followed by a noun phrase, it is a preposition and names the cause: 由于大雾，飞机没能起飞, 由于他的帮助，我很快找到了工作. It is more formal than 因为. The phrase usually opens the sentence, but it can also follow the subject: 他由于工作的原因常去外地.
The same word also links whole clauses (由于天气不好，……); that use is taught with the conjunctions.
The contrast example uses 为了 (in order to), from HSK 3: 为了不迟到，我早早就出门了. 为了 gives a purpose that lies ahead; 由于 gives a cause that already exists.
Common mistake: 由大雾，飞机没起飞. 由 alone means from or by; the cause needs 由于.

examples.text: 由于大雾，飞机没能起飞。
examples.reading: yóuyú dà wù, fēijī méi néng qǐfēi.
examples.translation: Because of the thick fog, the plane could not take off.

examples.text: 由于时间关系，我们就讲到这里。
examples.reading: yóuyú shíjiān guānxi, wǒmen jiù jiǎng dào zhèlǐ.
examples.translation: Because of the time, we will stop here.

examples.text: 由于他的帮助，我很快找到了工作。
examples.reading: yóuyú tā de bāngzhù, wǒ hěn kuài zhǎodào le gōngzuò.
examples.translation: Thanks to his help, I quickly found a job.

examples.text: 他由于工作的原因常去外地。
examples.reading: tā yóuyú gōngzuò de yuányīn cháng qù wàidì.
examples.translation: Because of his work he often travels to other cities.

examples.text: 运动会由于大雨改到了下周。
examples.reading: yùndònghuì yóuyú dà yǔ gǎi dào le xià zhōu.
examples.translation: The sports meeting was moved to next week because of the heavy rain.

examples.text: 为了不迟到，我早早就出门了。
examples.reading: wèile bù chídào, wǒ zǎozǎo jiù chūmén le.
examples.translation: So as not to be late, I left home early.

rows.label: 介词: 引出对象 (对于, 与)

lesson.title: 对于 and 与: regarding, with
lesson.summary: 对于 introduces the thing an attitude or opinion is about, and 与 is a formal 跟 or 和 that introduces the other party.
pattern: A + 对于 + N + Adj / V
A + 与 + B + V (见面 / 有关 / 不同)
body: 对于 (duìyú) introduces what an opinion, attitude or effect is about: 对于这个问题，大家的看法不同, 这本书对于初学者很有用. It can open the sentence or follow the subject: 他对于工作非常认真. In most of these sentences 对 also works.

与 (yǔ) is a written-style 跟: it introduces the other person or thing in 见面, 有关系, 不同 and similar expressions: 我要与王经理见面, 这件事与你没有关系, 今天的天气与昨天不同. The same 与 can also join two nouns as and; that use is taught with the conjunctions.
The contrast example uses 关于 (about, on the topic of), from HSK 3: 一篇关于环境保护的文章. 关于 names a topic and often forms 关于……的 before a noun; it cannot stand after the subject, so 这本书关于初学者很有用 is wrong.
Common mistake: 对于你没有关系. Relationships take 与 or 跟: 与你没有关系.

examples.text: 对于这个问题，大家的看法不同。
examples.reading: duìyú zhège wèntí, dàjiā de kànfǎ bù tóng.
examples.translation: People have different views on this question.

examples.text: 这本书对于初学者很有用。
examples.reading: zhè běn shū duìyú chūxuézhě hěn yǒuyòng.
examples.translation: This book is very useful for beginners.

examples.reading: tā duìyú gōngzuò fēicháng rènzhēn.
examples.translation: He is very conscientious about his work.

examples.reading: wǒ yào yǔ Wáng jīnglǐ jiànmiàn.
examples.translation: I am going to meet Manager Wang.

examples.reading: zhè jiàn shì yǔ nǐ méiyǒu guānxi.
examples.translation: This has nothing to do with you.

examples.text: 今天的天气与昨天不同。
examples.reading: jīntiān de tiānqì yǔ zuótiān bù tóng.
examples.translation: The weather today is different from yesterday.

examples.text: 他写了一篇关于环境保护的文章。
examples.reading: tā xiě le yì piān guānyú huánjìng bǎohù de wénzhāng.
examples.translation: He wrote an article about environmental protection.

rows.label: 介词: 引出凭借、依据 (作为, 按, 按照)

lesson.title: 作为 按 按照: as, according to
lesson.summary: 作为 means in the role of, and 按 / 按照 mean according to a rule, plan or order.
pattern: 按 / 按照 + rule / plan + V
body: 作为 (zuòwéi) names the role or identity from which someone speaks or acts: 作为学生，你应该好好学习, 作为朋友，我想提醒你一句. 按照 (ànzhào) means according to and goes before a rule, a plan or an instruction: 按照计划, 按照规定. 按 (àn) means the same and is common before short words and in spoken requests: 按顺序, 按我说的做.
The contrast example uses 按时 (on time), the time adverb: 飞机按时起飞了. 按时 is one word that goes straight before the verb; 按照 needs a noun after it, so 飞机按照起飞了 is wrong.
Common mistake: 按照他，这样不对. To give someone's opinion, say 在他看来 or 他认为; 按照 goes with rules and plans.

examples.text: 作为学生，你应该好好学习。
examples.reading: zuòwéi xuésheng, nǐ yīnggāi hǎohǎo xuéxí.
examples.translation: As a student, you should study hard.

examples.text: 作为朋友，我想提醒你一句。
examples.reading: zuòwéi péngyou, wǒ xiǎng tíxǐng nǐ yí jù.
examples.translation: As a friend, I want to give you a word of warning.

examples.reading: qǐng àn shùnxù páiduì.
examples.translation: Please queue in order.

examples.text: 我们按照计划完成了任务。
examples.reading: wǒmen ànzhào jìhuà wánchéng le rènwu.
examples.translation: We completed the task according to plan.

examples.text: 按照规定，这里不能抽烟。
examples.reading: ànzhào guīdìng, zhèlǐ bù néng chōuyān.
examples.translation: Under the rules, smoking is not allowed here.

examples.reading: nǐ jiù àn wǒ shuō de zuò ba.
examples.translation: Just do as I say.

examples.reading: fēijī ànshí qǐfēi le.
examples.translation: The plane took off on time.

rows.label: 连词: 连接词或词组 (并, 而, 与)

lesson.title: 并 而 与: joining verbs, adjectives and nouns
lesson.summary: 并 joins two verb phrases done by the same subject, 而 joins two adjectives, and 与 is a formal and between nouns.
body: Chinese uses different words for and depending on what is joined. 并 (bìng) joins two actions of one subject, the second following the first: 会议讨论并通过了这个计划. 而 (ér) joins two adjectives, in written style: 简单而有效, 聪明而可爱. 与 (yǔ) joins two nouns like 和, but is more formal: 老师与学生.
The contrast example uses 而且 (and also, moreover), from HSK 3: 这家店的菜便宜，而且很好吃. 而且 links two clauses and adds a further point; 与 cannot do that, so 便宜，与很好吃 is wrong.
Common mistake: 我喜欢唱歌与跳舞 is acceptable in writing, but 他聪明与可爱 is not: 与 joins nouns, not predicates. Use 他聪明而可爱 or 他又聪明又可爱.

examples.text: 会议讨论并通过了这个计划。
examples.reading: huìyì tǎolùn bìng tōngguò le zhège jìhuà.
examples.translation: The meeting discussed and approved the plan.

examples.text: 他听完并记下了老师的话。
examples.reading: tā tīng wán bìng jì xià le lǎoshī de huà.
examples.translation: He listened to the end and wrote down what the teacher said.

examples.reading: zhège fāngfǎ jiǎndān ér yǒuxiào.
examples.translation: This method is simple and effective.

examples.text: 她是一个聪明而可爱的女孩。
examples.reading: tā shì yí ge cōngming ér kě'ài de nǚhái.
examples.translation: She is a clever and lovely girl.

examples.text: 老师与学生都参加了比赛。
examples.reading: lǎoshī yǔ xuésheng dōu cānjiā le bǐsài.
examples.translation: Teachers and students both took part in the competition.

examples.text: 这家店的菜便宜，而且很好吃。
examples.reading: zhè jiā diàn de cài piányi, érqiě hěn hǎochī.
examples.translation: The food at this restaurant is cheap, and it tastes good too.

rows.label: 连词: 连接分句 (此外, 而, 既然, 甚至, 不过, 并且)

lesson.title: Clause links 此外 而 既然 甚至 不过 并且
lesson.summary: 此外 adds another point, 而 sets two facts against each other, 既然 starts from a known fact, 甚至 goes to an extreme, 不过 adds a mild but, and 并且 adds a further action.
body: 此外 (cǐwài) means besides, in addition, and is followed by a comma or a new clause: ……很近，此外，价格也不贵. 并且 (bìngqiě) means and also; it adds a second action or fact, often with the same subject: 他同意了，并且帮我说服了大家. 而 (ér) between clauses sets two subjects side by side in contrast: 哥哥喜欢安静，而弟弟喜欢热闹.

既然 (jìrán) starts from a fact both people accept and draws a conclusion or suggestion, usually with 就: 既然来了，就多住几天吧. 甚至 (shènzhì) means even, the extreme case: 他忙得甚至忘了吃饭. 不过 (búguò) is a softer but: 这个办法不错，不过有点儿麻烦.
The contrast example uses 因为 (because), from HSK 2: 因为堵车，他迟到了半个小时. 因为 simply gives a cause; 既然 needs a conclusion or suggestion after it, so it does not fit a plain report of what happened.
Common mistake: 既然下雨了，我昨天没去. 既然 leads to a decision, not a past report; say 因为下雨了，我昨天没去, or 既然下雨了，我们就别去了.

examples.text: 这家酒店离机场很近，此外，价格也不贵。
examples.reading: zhè jiā jiǔdiàn lí jīchǎng hěn jìn, cǐwài, jiàgé yě bú guì.
examples.translation: This hotel is close to the airport; besides, it is not expensive.

examples.text: 哥哥喜欢安静，而弟弟喜欢热闹。
examples.reading: gēge xǐhuan ānjìng, ér dìdi xǐhuan rènao.
examples.translation: The older brother likes quiet, whereas the younger one likes a lively scene.

examples.text: 既然来了，就多住几天吧。
examples.reading: jìrán lái le, jiù duō zhù jǐ tiān ba.
examples.translation: Since you are here, stay a few more days.

examples.reading: tā máng de shènzhì wàng le chīfàn.
examples.translation: He was so busy that he even forgot to eat.

examples.text: 这个办法不错，不过有点儿麻烦。
examples.reading: zhège bànfǎ búcuò, búguò yǒudiǎnr máfan.
examples.translation: This method is good, but it is a bit of a bother.

examples.text: 他同意了我的意见，并且帮我说服了大家。
examples.reading: tā tóngyì le wǒ de yìjiàn, bìngqiě bāng wǒ shuōfú le dàjiā.
examples.translation: He agreed with me and also helped me win everyone over.

examples.text: 因为堵车，他迟到了半个小时。
examples.reading: yīnwèi dǔchē, tā chídào le bàn ge xiǎoshí.
examples.translation: Because of a traffic jam, he was half an hour late.

rows.label: 连词: 连接分句 (不光, 不仅, 另外, 要是, 因此, 由于, 加)

lesson.title: Clause links 不光 不仅 另外 要是 因此 由于 加上
lesson.summary: 不光 and 不仅 mean not only, 另外 adds something else, 要是 means if, 因此 means therefore, 由于 gives a cause clause, and 加上 adds one more reason.
pattern: 不仅 / 不光 + A，还 / 也 / 而且 + B
由于 + cause，(因此) + result; reason 1，加上 + reason 2
body: 不仅 (bùjǐn) and its spoken twin 不光 (bùguāng) mean not only; the second clause adds with 还, 也 or 而且: 他不光会开车，还会修车. 另外 (lìngwài) means in addition and often stands alone before a comma: 我没时间，另外，我也不太想去. 要是 (yàoshi) is a spoken if, usually with 就 in the result.

由于 (yóuyú) followed by a whole clause gives the cause, and 因此 (yīncǐ) introduces the result: 由于工作太忙，他很久没回家了, 他每天锻炼，因此身体很好. 加 is used mostly as 加上 (on top of that), adding one more reason before the result: 路太远，加上又下雨，我们就没去.
The contrast example uses 而且 (moreover), from HSK 3, the usual partner of 不仅: 他不仅聪明，而且很努力. 而且 opens the second half; 不仅 opens the first.
Common mistake: 因此 at the start of the cause clause, as in 因此天气不好，比赛取消了. 因此 introduces the result; the cause takes 由于 or 因为.

examples.text: 他不光会开车，还会修车。
examples.reading: tā bùguāng huì kāichē, hái huì xiū chē.
examples.translation: He can not only drive but also repair cars.

examples.text: 不仅学生喜欢他，老师也喜欢他。
examples.reading: bùjǐn xuésheng xǐhuan tā, lǎoshī yě xǐhuan tā.
examples.translation: Not only do the students like him, the teachers do too.

examples.text: 我没时间，另外，我也不太想去。
examples.reading: wǒ méi shíjiān, lìngwài, wǒ yě bú tài xiǎng qù.
examples.translation: I have no time; besides, I do not really want to go.

examples.text: 要是有问题，随时给我打电话。
examples.reading: yàoshi yǒu wèntí, suíshí gěi wǒ dǎ diànhuà.
examples.translation: If there is a problem, call me any time.

examples.text: 他每天锻炼，因此身体很好。
examples.reading: tā měi tiān duànliàn, yīncǐ shēntǐ hěn hǎo.
examples.translation: He exercises every day, so he is very healthy.

examples.text: 由于工作太忙，他很久没回家了。
examples.reading: yóuyú gōngzuò tài máng, tā hěn jiǔ méi huí jiā le.
examples.translation: Because work has been so busy, he has not been home for a long time.

examples.text: 路太远，加上又下雨，我们就没去。
examples.reading: lù tài yuǎn, jiāshang yòu xià yǔ, wǒmen jiù méi qù.
examples.translation: It was too far, and on top of that it was raining, so we did not go.

examples.text: 他不仅聪明，而且很努力。
examples.reading: tā bùjǐn cōngming, érqiě hěn nǔlì.
examples.translation: He is not only clever but also hard-working.

rows.label: 其他助词 (等, 者, 之, 就是)

lesson.title: Particles 等 者 之 就是: and so on, the person who, of, that is all
lesson.summary: 等 ends a list (and so on), 者 makes a noun for a person who does something, 之 is a written of in set forms such as 之一 and 三分之一, and 就是 at the end of a sentence means that is all there is to it.
pattern: V / N + 者 (作者, 读者)
N + 之一; number + 分之 + number; clause + 就是 (了)
body: 等 (děng) after a list says there are more items like these, and can be followed by the general noun: 苹果、香蕉等水果. 者 (zhě) attaches to a verb or noun to make a word for the person: 作者 (author), 读者 (reader), 记者 (reporter). 之 (zhī) is a written-style 的 that survives in fixed forms: 学生之一 (one of the students), 三分之一 (one third).
就是 at the end of a sentence, often with 了, reassures: just do it and that is all: 这事你别管了，我来办就是了.
The contrast example uses the suffix 们, from HSK 1: 记者们都来了. 们 makes a person noun plural; 者 makes the person noun in the first place.
Common mistake: 三分的一. Fractions need 之: 三分之一.

examples.text: 我去超市买了苹果、香蕉等水果。
examples.reading: wǒ qù chāoshì mǎi le píngguǒ, xiāngjiāo děng shuǐguǒ.
examples.translation: I went to the supermarket and bought apples, bananas and other fruit.

examples.text: 这本书的作者是一位老师。
examples.reading: zhè běn shū de zuòzhě shì yí wèi lǎoshī.
examples.translation: The author of this book is a teacher.

examples.text: 这本杂志有很多年轻读者。
examples.reading: zhè běn zázhì yǒu hěn duō niánqīng dúzhě.
examples.translation: This magazine has many young readers.

examples.text: 他是我们班最好的学生之一。
examples.reading: tā shì wǒmen bān zuì hǎo de xuésheng zhī yī.
examples.translation: He is one of the best students in our class.

examples.reading: sān fēn zhī yī de tóngxué méi lái.
examples.translation: A third of the classmates did not come.

examples.text: 这事你别管了，我来办就是了。
examples.reading: zhè shì nǐ bié guǎn le, wǒ lái bàn jiùshì le.
examples.translation: Leave this to me; I will just take care of it.

examples.reading: jìzhěmen dōu lái le.
examples.translation: The reporters have all come.

rows.label: 叹词 (啊, 嗯)

lesson.title: Interjections 啊 and 嗯: surprise, asking again, agreeing
lesson.summary: 啊 at the start of a sentence shows surprise, realisation or a request to repeat, depending on its tone; 嗯 says yes, I see, or asks a puzzled question.
body: An interjection stands alone at the front of the sentence, followed by a comma, a question mark or an exclamation mark. 啊 changes meaning with its tone: ā shows surprise or admiration (啊，下雪了！), á asks someone to repeat (啊？你说什么？), à shows sudden understanding (啊，原来是你！). 嗯 with a falling tone, ǹ, says yes or I see (嗯，我知道了); with a rising tone, ń, it asks a puzzled question (嗯？他怎么还没来？).
The contrast example uses 啊 as a sentence-final particle, from HSK 1: 你快来啊！. At the end, toneless a softens or urges; at the front, with a tone, it is an interjection.
Common mistake: putting a particle such as 吗 or 呢 where the interjection goes, as in 吗？你说什么？. Particles only end sentences.

examples.reading: ā, xià xuě le!
examples.translation: Oh, it is snowing!

examples.reading: á? nǐ shuō shénme?
examples.translation: Huh? What did you say?

examples.reading: à, yuánlái shì nǐ!
examples.translation: Ah, so it is you!

examples.reading: ǹ, wǒ zhīdào le.
examples.translation: Mm, I see.

examples.reading: ń? tā zěnme hái méi lái?
examples.translation: Hm? Why has he still not come?

examples.reading: ǹ, zhège zhǔyi búcuò.
examples.translation: Mm, that is a good idea.

examples.reading: nǐ kuài lái a!
examples.translation: Come quickly!

rows.label: 结构类型 (数词 + 形容词 + 量词)

lesson.title: Number + adjective + measure word: 一大杯, 一小块, 一整天
lesson.summary: A few short adjectives such as 大, 小 and 整 can go between the number and the measure word: 一大杯水, 一小块蛋糕, 一整天.
pattern: number + 大 / 小 / 整 + MW + N
body: Between the number and the measure word, Chinese allows only a few one-syllable adjectives, mainly 大 (big), 小 (small) and 整 (whole): 一大杯水 (a big glass of water), 一小块蛋糕 (a small piece of cake), 一整天 (a whole day), 两大箱书 (two big boxes of books), 一大群孩子 (a big crowd of children).
The contrast example uses 很 + adjective + 的 after the measure word: 一个很大的房子. A longer or modified adjective cannot go between the number and the measure word; it follows the measure word with 的.
Common mistake: 一很大杯水 or 一漂亮件衣服. Only bare 大, 小, 整 and a few others go inside; say 一件很漂亮的衣服.

examples.text: 他一口气喝了一大杯水。
examples.reading: tā yìkǒuqì hē le yí dà bēi shuǐ.
examples.translation: He drank a big glass of water in one go.

examples.reading: wǒ zhǐ chī le yì xiǎo kuài dàngāo.
examples.translation: I only ate a small piece of cake.

examples.reading: wǒ děng le nǐ yì zhěng tiān.
examples.translation: I waited for you a whole day.

examples.reading: tā bān lái le liǎng dà xiāng shū.
examples.translation: He brought over two big boxes of books.

examples.reading: ménkǒu zhàn zhe yí dà qún háizi.
examples.translation: A big crowd of children is standing at the door.

examples.text: 他住在一个很大的房子里。
examples.reading: tā zhù zài yí ge hěn dà de fángzi li.
examples.translation: He lives in a very big house.

rows.label: 四字格 (一A一B, 无A无B, 有A有B)

lesson.title: Four-character frames 一A一B, 无A无B, 有A有B
lesson.summary: 一A一B shows wholeness or alternation (一模一样, 一问一答), 无A无B means without any (无忧无虑), and 有A有B means having both, full of life (有说有笑).
body: These frames put two related words into a fixed four-character shape. 一A一B expresses wholeness or two actions taking turns: 一模一样 (exactly alike), 一心一意 (wholeheartedly), 一问一答 (one asks, the other answers). 无A无B means completely without: 无忧无虑 (carefree), 无影无踪 (without a trace). 有A有B means having both, lively and full: 有说有笑 (chatting and laughing), 有声有色 (vivid).

Each expression is fixed: you cannot move A and B into another frame. The contrast example uses AABB reduplication, from HSK 3: 洗得干干净净. AABB repeats an adjective for vividness; it is not one of these frames, so 无干无净 is not a word.
Common mistake: making up a new four-character form by analogy, such as 有忧有虑. Learn each expression as a whole.

examples.text: 这对双胞胎长得一模一样。
examples.reading: zhè duì shuāngbāotāi zhǎng de yìmú-yíyàng.
examples.translation: These twins look exactly alike.

examples.text: 他一心一意地照顾生病的妈妈。
examples.reading: tā yìxīn-yíyì de zhàogù shēngbìng de māma.
examples.translation: He looks after his sick mother wholeheartedly.

examples.text: 两个孩子一问一答，说得很热闹。
examples.reading: liǎng ge háizi yí wèn yì dá, shuō de hěn rènao.
examples.translation: The two children took turns asking and answering, chatting away happily.

examples.text: 孩子们过着无忧无虑的生活。
examples.reading: háizimen guò zhe wúyōu-wúlǜ de shēnghuó.
examples.translation: The children live a carefree life.

examples.reading: xiǎotōu pǎo de wúyǐng-wúzōng.
examples.translation: The thief ran off without a trace.

examples.text: 大家坐在一起有说有笑。
examples.reading: dàjiā zuò zài yìqǐ yǒushuō-yǒuxiào.
examples.translation: Everyone sat together, chatting and laughing.

examples.text: 他讲故事讲得有声有色。
examples.reading: tā jiǎng gùshi jiǎng de yǒushēng-yǒusè.
examples.translation: He tells stories vividly.

examples.text: 妈妈把衣服洗得干干净净。
examples.reading: māma bǎ yīfu xǐ de gāngānjìngjìng.
examples.translation: Mum washed the clothes spotlessly clean.
